_meta.indication: GALAFOLD is indicated for the treatment of adults with a confirmed diagnosis of Fabry disease and an amenable galactosidase alpha gene (GLA) variant based on in vitro assay data.

pivotal_trials.design: Placebo-controlled, double-blind trial; patients randomized 1:1 to Galafold 123 mg orally once every other day or placebo for 6 months.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 16 years and older with Fabry disease who had an amenable (initially termed 'responsive') GLA variant based on an in vitro (CT HEK-293) assay.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy outcome: proportion of patients with >=50% reduction from baseline to month 6 in the average number of GL-3 inclusions per kidney interstitial capillary (KIC) in biopsy samples.
pivotal_trials.n: 67 patients enrolled (ITT; 43 females, 24 males); final efficacy population reduced to 50 (ITT-amenable) and 45 with available histology.
pivotal_trials.result: In the ITT population the primary outcome was achieved in 13 of 34 (38%) Galafold-treated vs 9 of 33 (27%) placebo patients (p=0.3). In the ITT-amenable population with available histology (N=45), 13 of 25 (52%) on Galafold vs 9 of 20 (45%) on placebo achieved the outcome.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) were headache (35% vs 21% placebo), nasopharyngitis (18% vs 6%), urinary tract infection (15% vs 0), nausea (12% vs 6%), and pyrexia (12% vs 3%). No deaths or serious adverse events were convincingly attributed to Galafold in phase 3 trials.
target_moa: Migalastat is a pharmacological chaperone that reversibly binds to the active site of alpha-galactosidase A (alpha-Gal A), stabilizing amenable mutant forms of the enzyme in the endoplasmic reticulum and facilitating their proper trafficking to lysosomes, where alpha-Gal A breaks down GL-3 and lyso-Gb3.

rems.type: A risk evaluation and mitigation strategy or REMS will not be required.

companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic was required; DNA sequencing of the GLA gene is part of the standard diagnostic workup in Fabry disease performed by commercial molecular genetics laboratories.

advisory_committee.vote: The application for Galafold was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Reduction in renal globotriaosylceramide (GL-3) deposition in kidney interstitial capillaries, a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: The Applicant has demonstrated the effect of Galafold on a surrogate endpoint (renal globotriaosylceramide, GL-3, deposition in kidney interstitial capillaries) that is reasonably likely, based on pathophysiologic data, to predict clinical benefit in adults with Fabry disease.

confirmatory_requirement.text: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (PMR 3412-1) to verify and describe the clinical benefit of Galafold in patients with Fabry disease and amenable, disease-causing GLA variants.

citations.quote: 3412-1 A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to verify and describe the clinical benefit of Galafold (migalastat) in patients with Fabry disease.

summary.text: Galafold received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 (subpart H) based on its effect on a surrogate endpoint (renal GL-3 deposition) reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with a required confirmatory trial. The application was a priority-review original submission and the drug has orphan drug designation in Fabry disease.

citations.quote: I concur with the recommendation of the Division of Gastroenterology and Inborn Errors Products (DGIEP) for accelerated approval for NDA 208623 Galafold (migalastat) under 21 CFR 314.510 (subpart H).

The Applicant has demonstrated the effect of Galafold on a surrogate endpoint (renal globotriaosylceramide, GL-3, deposition in kidney interstitial capillaries) that is reasonably likely, based on pathophysiologic data, to predict clinical benefit in adults with Fabry disease.

requirement.text: 3412-1: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to verify and describe the clinical benefit of Galafold in patients with Fabry disease and amenable, disease-causing GLA variants.

citations.quote: 3412-1 A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to verify and describe the clinical benefit of Galafold (migalastat) in patients with Fabry disease.

requirement.text: 3412-2: A prospective, longitudinal, observational study to evaluate the efficacy and pharmacodynamic effects of Galafold in patients with confirmed Fabry disease and amenable, disease-causing GLA variants, used to verify and describe clinical benefit.

citations.quote: 3412-2 A prospective, longitudinal, observational study to evaluate the efficacy and pharmacodynamic effects of Galafold (migalastat) in patients with a confirmed diagnosis of Fabry disease and amenable, disease-causing *GLA* variants.

requirement.text: 3412-3: A worldwide, prospective, single-arm, observational study in women exposed to Galafold during pregnancy and lactation to assess risks of pregnancy complications and adverse effects on the fetus/neonate and breastfed infant.

citations.quote: 3412-3 A worldwide, prospective, single-arm, observational study in women exposed to Galafold (migalastat) during pregnancy and lactation to assess: risks of pregnancy complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on lactation and the breastfed infant.

requirement.text: 3412-4: A PK/PD trial to evaluate an appropriate dosing regimen of Galafold in patients with Fabry disease and amenable GLA variants who have severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2) or who are on kidney dialysis.

citations.quote: 3412-4 A PK/PD trial to evaluate an appropriate dosing regimen of Galafold (migalastat) in patients with Fabry disease and amenable *GLA* variants who have severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2/year) or who are on kidney dialysis.

requirement.text: 3412-5: A study to generate additional DNA sequencing data for all recombinant GLA cDNA constructs used to generate in vitro alpha-Gal A enzyme data from HEK-293 cells in support of NDA 208623.
